place.why: The patient says the care was at the Royal Victoria Hospital Emergency Department in Belfast, and Belfast is in Northern Ireland.

summary: Royal Victoria Hospital is part of Belfast Health and Social Care Trust, so you complain to Belfast Trust first, usually within 6 months, using its online complaint form or other contact routes. If you are still unhappy after the Trust’s final response, the independent body is the Northern Ireland Public Services Ombudsman, but its online form page is currently down and it tells people to use email or phone instead. For compensation, the route we found is a clinical negligence court claim, usually via a solicitor, with a 3-year limitation period and possible legal aid subject to means and merits.

steps.body: Northern Ireland clinical negligence court route
steps.what: The compensation route we found for harm from public hospital care in Northern Ireland is a clinical negligence court claim, usually started through a solicitor. We did not find an official no-fault or redress scheme for this kind of hospital negligence in the official pages opened in this run.
steps.deadline: (4) Except where paragraph (5) applies, that period is three years from—
points: The limitation law says a personal injury action "may not be brought after the expiration of the period" and that period is "three years" from accrual or the later "date of knowledge" of the injured person.
An official Department of Health flyer says "you should make contact with a solicitor in the first instance".
The Department of Justice says clinical-negligence legal-aid certificates are often first limited to "investigation of the potential claim under the pre-action protocol".
The HSC Directorate of Legal Services says its Clinical Negligence Team is "the sole provider of advice, representation and training to the Public Health and Social Care sector in Northern Ireland."
steps.appliesIf: You want damages for injury or loss caused by negligent hospital care in Northern Ireland.
alternatives: Complaint to Belfast Trust and then NIPSO if you want answers, apology, or service learning rather than court damages.
missing: Your exact 'date of knowledge' if it differs from the treatment date.
Your evidence of losses, surgery, symptoms and missed work or coursework.

steps.body: Department of Justice / Legal Services Agency Northern Ireland
steps.what: Legal aid is available in Northern Ireland for clinical negligence claims, subject to means and merits, and the application is made by a solicitor through LAMS. For contentious court work, the solicitor legislation says an agreement for payment only if the case succeeds is not valid, so the usual 'no win no fee' success-only model is not allowed on the official wording we opened.
points: The Department says legal aid is available "subject to means and merits test".
For clinical negligence, the Department says: "You will need to make an application to representation higher."
The Department also says certificates are often first limited to "investigation of the potential claim under the pre-action protocol".
Financial eligibility is based on "disposable income and capital during the seven days up to and including the date of initial advice".
A solicitor must be "satisfied" about financial eligibility before applying on LAMS.
The solicitor legislation says a solicitor cannot stipulate for "payment only in the event of success in that action or proceeding" in contentious proceedings.
steps.appliesIf: Funding a Northern Ireland clinical negligence claim.
alternatives: Ask a solicitor whether any lawful alternative funding or legal-expenses insurance may apply.
missing: Your income, savings/capital and benefit details for legal aid.
Whether you have any legal-expenses insurance.

steps.body: The Law Society of Northern Ireland
steps.what: Patients can use the Law Society of Northern Ireland's solicitor directory to find a solicitor by place and by legal category. For a missed-fracture claim, the category 'Professional negligence' is the clearest directory match, with 'Accidents Including personal injuries' also potentially relevant.

steps.body: Department of Health Northern Ireland / NICE
steps.what: Clinicians in Northern Ireland use NICE clinical guidelines, with the Department of Health Northern Ireland setting the local endorsement, implementation, monitoring and assurance process.
points: NICE publishes the clinical guidelines.
The Department of Health says it has reviewed the process for their endorsement, implementation, monitoring and assurance in Northern Ireland.
The current arrangements are set out in a Department circular effective from 1 July 2026.
The guidance does not replace individual professional judgment for the patient in front of the clinician.
steps.appliesIf: Health and social care in Northern Ireland.

sources.quote: NICE Clinical Guidelines make evidence-based recommendations on a wide range of topics from preventing and managing specific conditions to planning broader services and interventions to improve the health of communities
The Department has reviewed its process for the endorsement, implementation, monitoring and assurance of NICE Clinical Guidelines in Northern Ireland.

The arrangements for the endorsement, implementation, monitoring and assurance of NICE Guidelines with a clinical focus in Northern Ireland are detailed in the following circular, which is effective from 1 July 2026.

steps.body: Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
steps.what: To get a copy of your own health and social care records from Belfast Trust, you ask in writing using the Trust's subject access route. The Trust points patients to a downloadable subject access application form rather than an online form.
steps.wall: The Trust provides a downloadable DOCX subject access application form rather than an online form.
points: The Trust says to submit the request in writing to the relevant department.
For community Health and Social Care records and other personal information requests, the page directs patients to the Data Protection Officer.
The page offers a downloadable 'subject access application form'.
After the Trust has all necessary documents and any fees, it says it has 30 days under UK GDPR to provide the information.
If the request is complex, it says it may take a further 60 days.
steps.appliesIf: Requests for your own personal information or health and social care records held by Belfast Trust.

sources.quote: Please submit your request in writing to the relevant department.
Or download the subject access application form.

When we have received all the necessary documentation and fees, we have 30 days under UK GDPR to provide the information requested. If the request is complex, we may have a further 60 days if necessary to respond.
